official_measurement_examples.name: 48 strategy areas
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 26 June 2026 official map identifies 48 LNRS areas covering England with no gaps or overlaps and names a responsible authority for each area.

official_measurement_examples.name: Publication status varies
official_measurement_examples.fact: The official responsible-authority list records whether individual strategies are published; draft and published strategies must remain temporally distinct.

official_measurement_examples.name: Required contents
official_measurement_examples.fact: Each LNRS must contain a local habitat map and a written statement of biodiversity priorities, with proposals for where recovery action could be most beneficial.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local planning authorities must have regard to relevant LNRS evidence, but an LNRS is not itself a planning permission or a development-plan allocation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Material consideration
official_measurement_examples.fact: Published LNRS information may be a material consideration depending on the circumstances of the case; mapped priority does not determine a planning outcome automatically.

official_measurement_examples.name: Draft evidence distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A consulted draft LNRS may contain useful evidence but must not be silently treated as the final published strategy.

official_measurement_examples.name: BNG relationship
official_measurement_examples.fact: LNRS can inform strategic significance in nature recovery and BNG delivery, but LNRS mapping does not itself approve a biodiversity gain plan or habitat intervention.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: LNRS priority mapping does not establish ownership planning permission exact buildable area ecological clearance or final development yield.

core_rules: LNRS is statutory strategy not planning permission
LNRS is not automatically a development-plan allocation
draft and published LNRS remain distinct
responsible authority status must be current
mapped priority is not automatic refusal
mapped priority is not ownership evidence
LNRS does not approve BNG plan
BNG strategic significance is not parcel permission
local habitat map is not cadastral boundary
LNRS does not replace protected-site law
LNRS does not calculate development yield
publication date and evidence lineage must remain distinct
no parcel LNRS clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
absence of mapped priority is not proof of no ecological constraint
